claims.statement: init, convert and format are directly dispatched local file-rewriting handlers that operate on working-directory paths without connector expansion or a preceding change into the connector's expanded directory.

Only validate and format are classified offline; init, convert and dump resolve credentials, construct SesamNode and pass the developer-mode gate before their handlers, and -force does not bypass that gate for them.

SesamNode construction attempts a portal analytics POST before creating the authenticated API connection when the JWT supplies a subscription identifier, so local preparation commands using online bootstrap can emit analytics even if the subsequent connection fails.
init, convert and format do not apply whitelist filtering to their file selection, unlike dump's archive selection.

dump replaces sesam-config.zip with a local archive of recursively selected pipe/system .conf.json files and optional node metadata, applying archive whitelist rules and regular-configuration Jinja substitution; convert's -dump calls this before conversion, but it does not back up testdata, expected output or profile environment files.

init scans immediate pipes/*.conf.json, excludes dataset, merge, merge_datasets, union_datasets, diff_datasets and embedded top-level sources, and wraps other non-conditional sources with fixed prod/original and test/empty-embedded alternatives selected by $ENV(node-env), independently of -profile.

For existing conditional sources, init adds an empty embedded test alternative only when test is missing and otherwise preserves the existing test source unless explicit sampling changes its entities.
init's live sampling is opt-in through -add-test-entities; existing nonempty test entities are protected unless -force-add is also set, and -force-add alone does not initiate sampling.

test_entities_to_pipe looks up the live pipe using the local JSON _id, samples its effective sink.dataset or fallback pipe ID with a limit of 10 and history/deleted/transit-decoding disabled, and stores those live entities inside source.alternatives.test.entities.

A missing remote pipe makes init sampling warn and return without adding entities, whereas a dataset-fetch exception warns and assigns an empty entities list; a forced refresh can therefore clear existing local entities even though the helper logs that test entities will not be updated.

init assumes source.type and compatible conditional alternatives; sampling an existing test alternative directly accesses its entities array, so a converted http_endpoint test branch without entities is not supported by init -add-test-entities.

init rewrites a pipe only when new_cfg is produced, using format_json with explicit UTF-8 output; it also writes an empty datatypes/additional_parameters manifest when not recognized as a connector and connector_dir is not '.'.

convert defaults to profile test and matches only a top-level conditional source whose alternative keyed by args.profile has type embedded; it neither evaluates condition nor reads profile environment data, and leaves other source variants or nonselected alternatives untouched.

For a matching source, convert extracts entities and replaces the entire selected embedded alternative with {'type': 'http_endpoint'}, preserving other alternatives and condition but not extra settings from the replaced branch.
convert rewrites the original configuration filename and creates testdata/<JSON _id>.json using format_json with explicit UTF-8, creating testdata on demand; the filename-derived ID helper is unused.

convert overwrites matching pipe and testdata files without prompts, merges or force checks; a subsequent conversion normally skips the now-http_endpoint branch and does not remove stale testdata, while another profile can target a different branch.

convert saves the modified pipe before its extracted data without transactional rollback, so a later data-write failure can leave an incomplete pair; empty entity arrays are written, but extracted None suppresses the data-file write.

convert interpolates JSON _id directly into its testdata path without normalization or collision checks, so matching duplicate IDs target the same output; malformed alternatives, missing entities, JSON errors or I/O errors can abort after earlier in-place rewrites.

The input-pipe-1 and input-pipe-2 conversion fixtures expect test embedded entities to become corresponding testdata files while prod remains a dataset source and literal condition 'test' remains unchanged.

The case-sensitive conversion fixture keeps configuration filename input-pipe-3.conf.json but uses JSON _id Input-Pipe-3 for testdata/Input-Pipe-3.json, preserving the case of entity IDs such as This, Pipe and PipeId.

The Norwegian conversion fixture expects testdata/input-pipe-norwegian.json from the JSON _id rather than input-pipe-with-norwegian-characters.conf.json's basename, and preserves literal øæå in both the pipe description and extracted entity names.
The conversion before/after fixtures leave a plain http_endpoint source, a conditional test http_endpoint source and the dataset-source output pipe unchanged.

format uses the first positional option or defaults to all; all formats immediate pipes, testdata, systems and expected *.json files in that order, folder modes use nonrecursive *.json globs, and grouped expected formatting skips paths containing .test.json whereas an explicit .json file is not skipped.
An unknown format option not ending in .json logs and returns rather than failing, but explicit-file read, JSON parse or write failures propagate to the normal CLI failure path.

Explicit-file formatting selects policy by splitting the supplied path on '/' and taking its first component matching an option key; only expected selects the expected-data serializer, and paths without a recognized component warn and use normal formatting, without case or OS-path normalization.

Expected-classified format files use standard json.dumps with two-space indentation, alphabetical keys and a final newline; Unicode remains literal unless -unicode-encoding is set, and <, > and & are escaped as \u003c, \u003e and \u0026 unless -disable-json-html-escape is set.

Normal format files use local format_json with conventional ordering, ensure_ascii=False and a trailing newline without expected-data HTML escape replacements; format uses text-mode opens with no explicit encoding, unlike init and convert's explicit UTF-8 writes.

The CLI imports its formatter from the locally owned jsonformat.py, whose header records a copy from Lake on 03/03/2025 during IS-18106; portal-equivalence is CLI help wording rather than a compatibility guarantee established by these local fixtures.

FormatStyle supplies defaults for omitted known keyword properties, and format_json/format_object default to FormatStyle instances: two-space non-tab indentation, colon/comma spaces, no newline-before-object options, nested-array closing newline and collapsed array-object indentation enabled, separate array-value lines disabled and conventional sorting enabled; font_size is stored but not used by the output formatter.

jsonformat recursively sorts mappings and mappings inside lists while preserving list element order; conventional keys lead according to _SORT_ORDER, other ordinary keys follow alphabetically, and internal underscore keys except _id plus $audit and $principals-from-user sort last; disabling conventional sorting makes key order alphabetical.

After compact Unicode-preserving JSON serialization, jsonformat's dictionary/array/string/escape state machine avoids treating quoted content as structural punctuation, collapses empty objects, avoids extra object indentation inside arrays by default, starts child arrays on new lines and applies the nested closing-array newline rule.

FormatStyle is available as a Python customization argument, but the inspected CLI passes no style to its rewriting calls and does not consume args.sesamconfig_file despite parsing -sesamconfig-file and README claims of .sesamconfig.json formatstyle customization; the fair-weather style fixture's separate-array-lines true does not change the current default.

format changes parsed JSON's representation without uploading, executing or verifying it, and does not reorder entity arrays or perform update/verify normalization; its expected serializer shares update's indentation/key/escaping policy but is not baseline generation or semantic verification.

The conversion scenario starts from a fresh copy of before, wipes a remote node, converts, runs test's upload/deployment-wait/run/verify lifecycle and resets the node; upload uses testdata filenames as pipe IDs and posts parsed entities after deployment, while the explicit expected spec covers output-pipe reading input-pipe-1 rather than separately asserting output for every converted fixture.

The conversion scenario's final diff -r against expected_after checks file-tree and byte-level representation expectations, including case and layout, separately from JSON semantic verification; authored extracted testdata uses the local collapsed array-object layout while expected output uses standard expanded indentation.

The conversion and fair-weather scenarios are not focused init or format tests; fair-weather exercises test, update, status and download and passes .mysesamconfig.json only to download, so it does not establish CLI style customization behavior.

The top-level test runner invokes scenario scripts using a remote CI token, and the CI OS matrix runs serially because its jobs share the same node, so these scenarios are remote, potentially destructive integration checks rather than harmless local diff scripts.
